conf.intro: Run the models on 10-second difficult clips from one file and judge by eye. Test clips stay in AnimeUp's cache: nothing here goes to the Finished videos folder.
conf.analisi: Analysing the source (10 to 50 seconds the first time, depending on resolution, then instant)...
conf.stat_episodio_aiuto: How long processing the whole episode would take with these settings. There are two figures because it depends on how many repeated frames deduplication finds: the minimum if it finds as many as an anime usually has, the maximum if it finds none.
conf.caso.sopra_spiega: The source has real detail to preserve: CUGAN keeps lines and textures that animevideov3 would smooth out.
conf.caso.mezzo_bloccato: In this range CUGAN light denoise is usually worth considering too, but from {h}p it can't reach {altezza}p with the current settings: animevideov3 remains the choice.
conf.caso.mezzo_spiega: There's no winner in this range: it depends on how dirty the original file is. animevideov3 is the baseline that gets the least wrong; if the file deserves more detail, check CUGAN light denoise below by picking a few clips and comparing these two models.
conf.caso.sotto_spiega: At this resolution there's hardly any genuine detail to preserve: what counts is the artefacts you avoid, and animevideov3 produces far fewer.
conf.regola_nota: This isn't theory: it comes from 1:1 comparisons of several real jobs.
conf.scansione: Scanning the source: under a minute...
conf.nessun_altro: There are no more clips different enough from the ones already found: the file is too short, or very similar to itself throughout.
conf.spiega_spezzoni: Clips are picked automatically where the models behave differently: still scenes (textures and banding), fast motion (flicker), dark scenes (gradients) and bright ones (sharp edges).
conf.nessuno_spezzone: No clips found: the file is too short.
conf.nota_sconsigliate: Note: {modelli} can still be selected, but isn't recommended for this file.
conf.includi_aiuto: Without a reference you can't tell real detail from detail the model made up.
conf.seleziona: Select at least one clip and one model.
conf.pronto: Comparison ready: the clips are below ↓
conf.dedup.storico: {pct} expected, from previously processed files of similar length
conf.dedup.ignota: on but not yet quantified, so it will finish sooner
conf.spiega_dettaglio: Fine detail: how much micro-structure there is compared with the upscaled original, which counts as 100%. Above 100% the model rebuilt edges that plain upscaling didn't have; below, it lost them, which is the plastic look. Between two models what matters is the GAP: a few points aren't visible to the eye, double is.
conf.spiega_rumore: Noise in flat areas: the same measure, but only where the image is nearly uniform — solid black, blown-out areas and flat colour fills excluded, since every model would score zero there. Above 100% the model adds grain or halos, below it cleans up: neither is better in absolute terms, it depends on how dirty the source is.
conf.proiezione: The full-episode projection factors in deduplication ({come}). The clip is one of the hardest in the file, so the real pace over the rest of the episode is usually a little better.
conf.ind_no_rif: Image indicators unavailable: they need the frames of the upscaled original as a baseline, and this comparison doesn't include it.
conf.ind_no_aree: Image indicators unavailable: this frame has no areas uniform enough to measure. The actual-size comparison is still below.
conf.avvertenza: Take them for what they are: there's no high-resolution original to compare against — pixels are being invented — so more detail doesn't mean more faithful. They rank the models against each other on this frame rather than scoring them, and a different scene can turn them around. Your eye is the judge: the actual-size comparison is below.
conf.risultati_nota: The files are in {cartella}/. Judge motion in video-compare, which opens with one click: the crops below are at native size, for a quick look.
conf.ritagli_nota: Actual-size crops (1:1). If the sheet doesn't fit the box, open it separately: shrinking it would make it useless.
conf.gia_in_corso: A comparison is already running: wait for it to finish, or stop it.
conf.fermato: Comparison stopped. The clips already processed are kept: click the button again to finish the rest.
conf.interrotto: The last comparison was cut short (the Mac was shut down, or the process ended). The clips already processed are kept: click “{pulsante}” to finish the rest.
conf.modelli_nota: Tick the ones to run on the clips. The recommended one is ticked for you.
conf.solo_scala: Works at {scala}× only: {altezza}p from this file
conf.clip_nota: Two are usually enough: one Motion plus one Static or Dark.
conf.trova_spiega: AnimeUp scans the whole file for motion and brightness, then picks up to eight 10-second clips where the models differ most: two each of Motion, Static, Dark and Bright. Under a minute; the scan is saved.
conf.prova_nota: Runs in the background: switch tabs, reload or close the window, and it carries on. Settings are locked until it ends. Stop keeps the versions already rendered.
conf.risultati_testo: {clip} × {modelli}. Judge motion side by side; the crops are at actual size.
conf.proiezione_breve: Projection uses dedup {pct}, {come}. This is one of the hardest clips, so the real pace is usually a little better.
conf.tacca: The tick marks 100%. More detail doesn't mean more faithful: pixels are being invented. Your eye is the judge.
conf.guarda: Watch in motion · opens in video-compare or IINA
conf.fermo_nota: Scroll sideways; never scaled, so artefacts stay visible.
conf.pronto_nota: Compare doesn't set anything: pick the model for each file in Processing.
conf.occupato: Something else is using the GPU right now: compare when it has finished, so the timings are true.
